title: State Department tour of South America in 1958
summary: A three-and-a-half-month tour in which the State Department used the band poorly, sometimes giving one concert a week.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: All right. Let's jump back out to the '50s for a moment. You had a major tour, didn't you, for the State Department to South America?
Yes, we went to South American in 1958, and it was a very lengthy tour, about three and a half months.
Was that your first one out of the country?
On a State Department kind of --

For the State Department, yes. And it was an interesting tour. However, unfortunately our State Department people, at least during that period, were not very well equipped to get the most good out of having someone like
ourselves there. They didn't really know how to --
-- approach it from an impresario department. And so very often, we'd go for a week and maybe do one concert in a whole week.
Of course, that made it an interesting tour.
Was this the one -- did you have Tito Puente down there at all? Was he down there at all?
No. No, all my association with Tito has been in New York.
